style: Defensively organised and disciplined under Amir Ghalenoei, Asia's second-highest-ranked side absorbs pressure in a compact block and counters through Taremi's hold-up play and wide runners.
recent_form: Comfortable AFC qualification as one of Asia's most consistent teams. Enter as the highest-ranked side in their group behind only Japan among Asian nations.

key_players.name: Mehdi Taremi
key_players.note: Olympiacos forward and undisputed attacking focal point; 60+ international goals with European pedigree from Porto and Inter.

key_players.name: Alireza Jahanbakhsh
key_players.note: Leads from wide areas; former Eredivisie top scorer with Premier League and Feyenoord experience.

key_players.name: Mehdi Ghayedi
key_players.note: Pacey, direct forward adding width and a goal threat in transition.

key_players.name: Saeid Ezatolahi
key_players.note: Physical screening midfielder providing balance in front of the back line.

key_players.name: Alireza Beiranvand
key_players.note: Experienced, commanding shot-stopper and long-time national number one.

historical_news: Iran enter as the second-highest-ranked Asian side, behind only Japan.
Sardar Azmoun omitted from the squad amid reports of a fallout with authorities.
Coach Amir Ghalenoei named a squad built around veterans Taremi and Jahanbakhsh.
Drawn in Group G with Belgium, Egypt and New Zealand.
Taremi, with 60+ international goals, central to Iran's hopes of a first knockout-stage run.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Respect for Iran's ranking and defensive solidity mixed with debate over the Azmoun omission and perennial questions about converting solid play into a knockout breakthrough.
